display.title: Vesamachta Bechagecha: The Joy of Sukkos and Dancing with the Torah
display.summary_short: Why Sukkos is 'your own holiday', and how on Simchas Torah the Torah itself asks to join our dancing and blesses us with health.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show on Chol HaMoed Sukkos. Uncle Yossi explains the command 'vesamachta bechagecha', rejoice in your festival: Sukkos is not only a memory of the past but our very own holiday, given to us by Hashem every year. There are many reasons for joy: sitting in the sukkah, shaking the lulav and esrog with the hadassim and aravos, and the Ushpizin, seven great guests who visit each night, each with his own night. Then comes Simchas Torah, when we finish reading the Torah and begin again, and dance with the Torah during Hakafos. The Torah has no feet, hands or mouth, so it asks to join our dance, and in return blesses us with a healthy body all year. Even the youngest can hold a handle or the mantle, and everyone should come on time and resolve to learn more Torah.
display.lesson: Be truly happy on Yom Tov, and hold on to the Torah when you dance on Simchas Torah.
